description: Scaffold Astro 7 (TypeScript strict, official blog template), configure the content collection schema, migrate both real posts (frontmatter + body, with images), and build out the SEO/performance/accessibility infrastructure (consts, BaseHead meta tags, RSS, sitemap, about/404 pages, nav, skip link, landmarks, alt text, contrast spot-check). This feature produces a fully working, buildable Astro site living alongside the still-present Jekyll source tree (which FEAT-002 removes later). Independent of FEAT-002 in content, but must run first since FEAT-002's cleanup step depends on this feature's extraction being complete.
steps: Confirm a supported Node version is active (Astro 7 needs ^18.20.8 || ^20.3.0 || >=22.0.0; the ambient default v10.24.1 will not work) - switch via nvm or equivalent before any npm command.

Run `npm create astro@latest --help` to verify current CLI flags against what design.md recorded (create-astro@5.3.0 at design time), then scaffold into the worktree root: `npm create astro@latest . -- --template blog --typescript strict --no-install --no-git` (adjust flags if the CLI has changed; if the `blog` template no longer exists, fall back to `--template minimal` and hand-port content collections/RSS/sitemap per design.md section 1). Run `npm install` afterward.

Determine whether the scaffold produced `src/content.config.ts` or `src/content/config.ts` and edit only that file to add the full schema from design.md section 2: title (string), description (string), pubDate (coerced date), updatedDate (optional coerced date), heroImage (optional, via the schema's image() helper), tags (string array, default []), categories (string array, default []), author (string, default 'Marcelo Ohashi'), draft (boolean, default false).

Set `site: 'https://mohashi.io'` in astro.config.mjs and add the @astrojs/sitemap integration (`npx astro add sitemap` or manual install + config). Confirm the template's existing src/pages/rss.xml.js (or .ts) points at the blog collection; update site title/description strings inside it if hardcoded instead of imported from consts.

Create src/consts.ts: SITE_TITLE='DevMode', SITE_DESCRIPTION='Exchange of developer insights - by Marcelo Ohashi', SITE_AUTHOR='Marcelo Ohashi', SITE_URL='https://mohashi.io', DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE='/images/me.jpeg', SOCIAL={twitter:'mgohashi', github:'mgohashi', instagram:'mohashi_', linkedin:'mohashi'}.

Copy assets/images/me.jpeg -> public/images/me.jpeg, assets/images/favicon.png -> public/favicon.png, and CNAME (content 'mohashi.io') -> public/CNAME. Do not delete the originals yet (FEAT-002 handles deletion).

Migrate the Knative post into src/content/blog/quick-start-knative/index.md: frontmatter per design.md's concrete block (title 'Quick Start Knative', description from the Jekyll `excerpt`, pubDate 2020-04-18, heroImage './knative.png', the tags/categories arrays copied verbatim from _posts/2020-04-18-setup-a-cloud-native-quarkus-app-in-knative.md). Port the body: strip `{: .notice}`/`{: .notice--info}`/`{: .notice--warning}` Kramdown IALs (convert meaningful ones to `> **Note**` blockquotes), replace the `{% include video id="KyCbkXF3Qpw" provider="youtube" %}` include (~line 486) with an accessible lazy-loaded iframe or a small YouTubeEmbed component, strip all 10 `{:target="_blank"}` occurrences, and rewrite footnotes `[^1]`/`[^2]` (lines 496-497) as inline parenthetical links. Copy knative.png, quakus-app-web-browser.png, and unsplash-image-1.jpg from assets/images/setup-a-cloud-native-quarkus-app-in-knative/ into the new post directory; deliberately do NOT copy quickstart-knative-webconsole.gif (orphaned, discard per design.md section 8).

Migrate the Tekton/pipelines post into src/content/blog/how-to-build-cloud-native-pipelines/index.md: frontmatter per design.md's concrete block (title 'How to build cloud-native pipelines', pubDate 2020-05-26, heroImage './tekton.png', tags/categories copied verbatim from _posts/2020-05-26-how-to-build-cloud-native-pipeline.md). Port the body: strip all 11 `{: .notice}` IALs (convert meaningful ones to blockquotes), strip all 24 `{:target="_blank"}` occurrences, strip the two `{: .align-center}` IALs on the gif images (~lines 710, 758) and leave those two gifs as plain `` (not astro:assets, per design.md section 5's animated-GIF exception), and remove the `` comment. Copy all 12 files from assets/images/how-to-build-cloud-native-pipeline/ into the new post directory.

Extend the shared head component (BaseHead.astro or the template's equivalent) with: canonical link from Astro.site + Astro.url.pathname; favicon link to /favicon.png; full OG tags (og:title, og:description, og:type, og:url, og:image, og:site_name) and Twitter Card tags (twitter:card=summary_large_image, twitter:site=@mgohashi, twitter:title, twitter:description, twitter:image); resolve heroImage to an absolute URL via `heroImage.src` directly (per the design review's NIT, matching the official template's own BaseHead.astro pattern - not getImage()) combined with `new URL(...).href` against Astro.site, falling back to DEFAULT_OG_IMAGE when no heroImage is present; add the RSS `<link rel="alternate">` tag.

Verify (and fix if needed) that the sitemap excludes the 404 page: after a build, grep dist/sitemap*.xml for '404'; if it appears, add a `filter` option excluding it to the @astrojs/sitemap integration config.

Create src/pages/about.astro (shared layout, body copy from _pages/about.md) and update src/pages/404.astro with the copy from _pages/404.md ('Page not found. Your pixels are in another canvas.') - do NOT port the fixurl.js script block.

Add two hardcoded nav links (Posts, About - Categories/Tags explicitly out of scope per design.md section 8) to the base layout's <nav>, and add a visually-hidden-until-focused 'Skip to content' link as the first focusable element pointing at #main-content on <main>, porting the intent of the Jekyll _includes/skip-links.html. Confirm semantic <header>/<nav>/<main id="main-content">/<footer> landmarks, a single <h1> per post page, and body headings starting at <h2>.
Spot-check color contrast of the template's default theme with a contrast-ratio tool, and write real descriptive alt text (not filenames) for every image reference in both migrated posts.
Replace .gitignore with the Astro-standard set from design.md section 9: dist/, .astro/, node_modules/, .env, .env.production, .DS_Store.
Commit the new Astro source tree locally on the existing `migrate-astro` branch (the Jekyll files remain untouched and still present - do not delete or stage deletions in this feature).
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` succeeds with exit code 0
dist/sitemap-index.xml (or sitemap-0.xml) exists and does not contain a 404 entry
dist/about/index.html contains the About page copy and dist/404.html contains the 404 copy without any fixurl.js script
Both post pages in dist/ contain og:title, og:description, and og:image meta tags, and exactly one rel="canonical" link each
dist/CNAME exists with content 'mohashi.io'; dist/favicon.png and dist/images/me.jpeg exist
Neither migrated post page's HTML contains an empty alt="" attribute on a content image
Each post page's HTML contains exactly one <h1> and an element with id="main-content"
verification: npm install && npm run build — confirm exit code 0
grep -o '<meta property="og:[a-z:]*"' dist/posts/quick-start-knative/index.html and the pipelines post — confirm og:title/og:description/og:image present
grep 'rel="canonical"' on both post pages — confirm exactly one match each
grep -c '404' dist/sitemap-index.xml (or sitemap-0.xml) — confirm it returns 0
grep -q 'software architect' dist/about/index.html and grep -q 'another canvas' dist/404.html
grep -c 'alt=""' on both post pages — confirm 0
grep -c '<h1' on both post pages — confirm 1 each; grep -q 'id="main-content"' on both — confirm present
cat dist/CNAME — confirm content is exactly 'mohashi.io'
findings:
All acceptance criteria and verification steps pass (npm run build exit 0 from a clean rm -rf dist .astro node_modules && npm install; both post pages, sitemap without a 404 entry, rss.xml with 2 items, about/404 content, og:title/og:description/og:image + exactly one canonical per post page, dist/CNAME='mohashi.io', dist/favicon.png, dist/images/me.jpeg, no alt="" on content images, exactly one

and id="main-content" per post page all verified directly against dist/ output). Environment/tooling drift from design.md (re-verified at implementation time, as design.md anticipated): - create-astro is still exactly 5.3.0 as design.md recorded, and the `blog` template still exists, but its CLI flags changed: `--typescript strict` no longer exists (the blog template now ships `astro/tsconfigs/strict` by default, so no flag is needed) and `--no-install`/`--no-git` are correct. Actual scaffold command used: `npx create-astro@5.3.0 . --template blog --no-install --no-git --yes`. - create-astro@5.3.0 itself requires Node >=22.22.0 (fails under Node 20 with EBADENGINE), which is narrower than design.md's astro-package engine range (^18.20.8 || ^20.3.0 || >=22.0.0). The installed astro@7.4.1's own package.json also now declares engines.node >=22.22.0, not the broader range design.md recorded at design time. FEAT-002's deploy.yml / withastro/action Node setup should target Node 22.22+, not just 'a supported Node in the stated range' - 18.x and plain 20.x will not work with what is actually installed today. - create-astro refused to scaffold into a non-empty directory (the Jekyll files are present) and instead created a subdirectory (randomly named, e.g. 'celestial-chaos'); I moved its contents up into the worktree root by hand (astro.config.mjs, package.json, package-lock.json, public/, src/, tsconfig.json, .vscode/{extensions,launch}.json) and discarded the scaffold's own README.md/AGENTS.md/.gitignore/placeholder favicon.ico+svg/blog-placeholder-*.jpg images, replacing .gitignore with design.md section 9's exact content. Renamed package.json's "name" from the random scaffold name to "mohashi-io". - Content collection config landed at src/content.config.ts (Astro 5+ convention), confirmed to be the template's actual convention - no src/content/config.ts was created. - Both posts used .mdx (not .md): the Knative post needed a Astro component import (plain .md can't import components), and the pipelines post needed raw tags for its 3 animated GIFs to bypass Astro's automatic markdown-image optimization pipeline (plain ![]() syntax on a relative path is auto-optimized even inside .md/.mdx, which would have converted them to static webp and broken the animation - confirmed by an initial build that reduced one GIF to a non-animated webp before I caught and fixed it). Note the pipelines post actually has 3 animated GIFs needing this treatment (eventlistener-tkn-log.gif, pipelinerun-tkn-log.gif, webconsole-pipelinerun-logs.gif), not the 2 design.md's step list named - the third was a markdown-syntax reference to pipelinerun-tkn-log.gif that needed the same raw- fix. - Added a heroImageAlt optional string field to the content collection schema (not in design.md's original field list) so each post's hero gets real descriptive alt text instead of the template's hardcoded alt="" - design.md section 6 called for exactly this ('alt derived from a required alt frontmatter-adjacent field passed at usage site, not stored in the schema itself') but a plain Zod object schema silently drops unrecognized frontmatter keys, so the field had to be added to the schema (as optional) for it to reach the layout at all. - The scaffolded Header.astro/Footer.astro shipped with the Astro template's own placeholder social links (astro.build's Mastodon/Twitter/GitHub, target="_blank", and Footer's literal 'Your name here' copyright text) - these aren't from Jekyll and design.md's steps didn't call them out explicitly, but shipping them as-is would have put a competing project's social links and placeholder text on a production site, and also reintroduced target="_blank" that the design explicitly drops everywhere else. Replaced with SITE_AUTHOR/SOCIAL from consts.ts (Twitter, GitHub, LinkedIn; dropped Mastodon since it's not in SOCIAL) with no target="_blank". Verified 0 occurrences of target="_blank" remain on either post page. - withastro/action version: design.md recorded v6.1.3 as current at design time; I did not re-verify this against the action's current tag since FEAT-002 owns deploy.yml, but flagging that the same re-verify-at-implementation-time caveat design.md states for this action applies there, and that action's Node setup should be checked against the >=22.22.0 constraint above, not the broader range. - Rewrote src/pages/index.astro (the landing page) to list real posts instead of the template's Astro-branded placeholder copy ('Hello, Astronaut!' etc.) - not explicitly itemized in FEAT-001's steps, but leaving placeholder marketing copy as the site's homepage would not be a working migration. - Permalinks use /posts/:slug/ throughout (nav, rss.xml link, posts index links) per design.md section 4's decision; the scaffold's default /blog/ path was renamed everywhere it appeared (src/pages/blog -> src/pages/posts, Header nav link, rss.xml link, posts/index.astro links).
